v1.feedback: The calyx-to-ratatouille color swerve is tasteful — aubergine/courgette/tomato are well-chosen and restrained — but the geometric transformation is too timid to read as confit byaldi plating. The ring displacement amplitude (0.4) and shallow dish depth (1.2) mean the 'surprise' phase looks like a slightly wobbly calyx with new colors, not a recognizable spiral of vegetable slices. To land the idea: increase ring discretization (use floor/step on radius to get hard concentric bands, not a soft sine), boost the spiral displacement so slices visibly overlap like shingles, and deepen the dish profile so the silhouette clearly shifts from tulip-cup to wide skillet. The color bands should lock to discrete rings rather than blending continuously — that tiled, alternating-slice read is the whole visual joke of the dish.

v2.feedback: The confit byaldi concept clearly drove the design — discrete vegetable-slice rings, spiral shingle offsets, skillet dish profile, piperade sauce base color — but the final form reads as a shallow colored bullseye, not a recognizable dish. Give the shingle tilt more amplitude (3.0+) and exaggerate the z-separation between rings so individual slices pop as overlapping discs when orbited; right now the 1.8 tilt vanishes into the -3.5 skillet depth. The four-color vegetable palette is well-chosen but needs more value contrast at the ring boundaries — add a thin dark gap (discard particles where ringFrac < 0.05) so slices read as discrete objects rather than painted bands.
